note: Both sets capture the core facts (Nitinol wire actuator, horizontal louvered configuration, 20% operable glazing on the southern façade, latent solar energy as the driving source), but A additionally records the material identity facts — Flexinol® as a trade name for Nitinol wire and its classification as a shape memory alloy (SMA) — which B omits. B's claims are otherwise well bound and it usefully records that the rotational movement 'requires no additional energy sources', a fact A drops. However, B duplicates the actuation-method and 20% glazing facts and alters two quotes ('southern façade' where the page reads 'south façade'), while A's only real weakness is loosely calling 'phototrophic movement' the actuation method. On balance A covers more of the page's engineering content with fewer quote and duplication problems.
remarks: Both sets state the 20% glazing fact twice (once as 'proportion', once as 'area' — the page gives only a percentage, not an area). B also states the actuation method twice (once with the Nitinol actuator, once without). Both sets miss the stated functions of the screens (insulate from direct solar radiation, control reflected light, allow cross ventilation, maintain privacy) and the fact that the movement closes the horizontal louvers; A additionally misses 'requires no additional energy sources', B misses the Flexinol®/Nitinol trade-name and SMA facts.
